newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, with most traders sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said on Monday.

"Rates were marked up slightly in the morning on some speculative shortcovering interest. There's no fresh news but everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from the outcome of Tuesday's meeting of the (U.S.) Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) and (March) consumer confidence data. Activity was centred at the short end due to settlement dates and the closure of books in the Japanese market," a local dealer said.
"I think rates will hover around here for the time being as all eyes are on Tuesday's FOMC meeting," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent, Tuesday/Wednesday rose 3/16 point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 and week-fixed rose 3/8 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/6 5-15/16 but twelve-months was unchanged from last Friday's 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent.
